title: Amazon revamps its e-commerce empire as data center power gets tight
excerpt: Amazon is spreading e-commerce workloads across more AWS regions as power and capacity constraints reshape cloud computing in the AI era.
content_html:
Exclusive

An industrywide power crunch is changing how Amazon runs its e-commerce empire

By Eugene Kim

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Amazon's huge e-commerce business is redesigning its cloud setup as power and data center capacity become increasingly constrained.

The multiyear effort, known internally as "Region Flex," aims to reduce the concentration of Amazon's online retail operations in a handful of large AWS regions and run systems across more locations at a smaller scale, according to internal planning documents obtained by Business Insider.

Internal plans include efforts to reduce Amazon e-commerce footprint in major AWS hubs such as Northern Virginia and Dublin, Ireland, according to the documents.

The AI boom has sparked an industrywide scramble for power and computing capacity. Amazon is racing to expand AWS data centers and says it added more capacity globally than any other company last year. Even so, CEO Andy Jassy said last month that AWS still can't build capacity fast enough to meet demand.

"AWS power constraints"

Region Flex may not have started due to industrywide power constraints caused by the AI boom, but the internal documents obtained by Business Insider show this has become a driving force behind the project.

The Amazon internal documents explicitly cite power and capacity constraints in its cloud planning for the e-commerce business.

One planning document from last year said online retail teams were investing in moving infrastructure out of AWS's Dublin region "to mitigate expansion risk due to AWS power constraints."

A separate online grocery team document said Region Flex was required to ensure Amazon could meet "projected capacity requirements in each region."

Amazon's e-commerce logistics organization described Region Flex as dividing its "service architecture footprint" so it could run "in more AWS regions at a smaller scale, in closer proximity to our customers," according to one planning document from earlier this year.

'S-Team goal'

Region Flex is being tracked by Amazon's most senior leaders.

Amazon's grocery business described the initiative as an "S-Team goal," referring to Amazon's senior leadership team, and said teams were planning more than 100 software migrations. The documents also describe Region Flex as improving resilience during AWS disruptions.

The industrywide AI boom has sent demand for computing infrastructure soaring while electricity and available data center space have become major constraints on expansion.

Vacancy rates across North America's largest data center markets fell to a record 1.4% at the end of 2025, according to CBRE. Limited power availability is pushing more data centers beyond established hubs into smaller markets where electricity can be secured more quickly.

Amazon is adding enormous amounts of infrastructure to meet demand. In October, the company said it had added more than 3.8 gigawatts of data center capacity over the previous year, doubling its cloud scale since 2022, and expects to roughly double its power capacity again by the end of 2027.

Distributing workloads

Dublin has been one focus of Region Flex. Ireland became one of Europe's biggest data center markets over the past decade, putting significant pressure on the country's electricity system.

An internal plan last year called for reducing the Dublin infrastructure footprint of Amazon's e-commerce operation by 40% through migrations and deprecations in 2025. It also contemplated fully moving away from Dublin by the end of 2026 and from AWS regions in Northern Virginia and Oregon by 2029.

In an email to Business Insider, an Amazon spokesperson confirmed Region Flex. The spokesperson added that official internal Amazon documents don't always reflect current plans and described some of the timelines and other details in the documents obtained by Business Insider as "not accurate."

"Evolving our infrastructure is nothing new — it's something we've done for years to deliver the experience our customers expect from Amazon," the spokesperson said.

Using more AWS regions gives Amazon's online retail business greater flexibility to meet customer demand, improve reliability, manage costs, and bring services closer to customers, according to the spokesperson.

The internal documents show Amazon moving workloads from its long-established Dublin hub and distributing them across more AWS regions, including Frankfurt and Zaragoza, Spain.

That can be more expensive. Some services moving from Dublin into those two other regions could see infrastructure costs rise 10% to 15%, according to one document, because distributing workloads can reduce hosting efficiency. Amazon also estimated $90 million in one-time spending on Region Flex in 2025, according to an internal planning document.

Distributing workloads doesn't necessarily eliminate capacity problems. One of the documents noted "capacity constraints" in the Zaragoza region meant the organization planned to move only 65% of its remaining infrastructure costs there, leaving 35% in Dublin.

Despite AWS's rapid expansion, the company still expects shortages to persist. Jassy called power the "single biggest constraint" last year, and said demand will continue to outstrip supply during last month's earnings call.

"Even at that amount, we will still not have enough capacity to meet all the demand we have in 2026," Jassy said, adding that he expected the same dynamic in 2027.

sentences.zh: 内部文件显示，亚马逊将工作负载从其历史悠久的都柏林中心转移，并将其分布到更多 AWS 区域，包括法兰克福和西班牙萨拉戈萨。

blocks.html_en: That can be more expensive. Some services moving from Dublin into those two other regions could see infrastructure costs rise 10% to 15%, according to one document, because distributing workloads can reduce hosting efficiency. Amazon also estimated $90 million in one-time spending on Region Flex in 2025, according to an internal planning document.

blocks.html_en: Distributing workloads doesn't necessarily eliminate capacity problems. One of the documents noted "capacity constraints" in the Zaragoza region meant the organization planned to move only 65% of its remaining infrastructure costs there, leaving 35% in Dublin.

全行业的电力紧缩正在改变亚马逊运营其电子商务帝国的方式

作者：Eugene Kim 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

随着电力和数据中心容量变得越来越有限，亚马逊庞大的电子商务业务正在重新设计其云设置。

根据 Business Insider 获得的内部规划文件，这项内部称为“Region Flex”的多年努力旨在减少亚马逊在线零售业务在少数几个大型 AWS 区域的集中度，并以较小的规模在更多地点运行系统。

文件显示，内部计划包括努力减少亚马逊在弗吉尼亚州北部和爱尔兰都柏林等主要 AWS 中心的电子商务足迹。

人工智能的繁荣引发了全行业对电力和计算能力的争夺。 亚马逊正在竞相扩展 AWS 数据中心，并表示去年其在全球范围内增加的容量比任何其他公司都多。 即便如此，首席执行官安迪·贾西（Andy Jassy）上个月表示，AWS 仍然无法足够快地建设容量来满足需求。

“AWS 功率限制”

Region Flex可能由于AI热潮导致全行业的电力限制而没有启动，但Business Insider获得的内部文件显示，这已成为该项目背后的驱动力。

亚马逊内部文件明确指出了其电子商务业务云规划中的电力和容量限制。

去年的一份规划文件称，在线零售团队正在投资将基础设施迁出 AWS 都柏林地区，“以减轻由于 AWS 电力限制而带来的扩张风险”。

一份单独的在线杂货团队文件称，需要区域弹性来确保亚马逊能够满足“每个地区的预计容量要求”。

根据今年早些时候的一份规划文件，亚马逊的电子商务物流组织将 Region Flex 描述为划分其“服务架构足迹”，以便它可以“以较小的规模在更多 AWS 区域中运行，更靠近我们的客户”。

“S队目标”

亚马逊最高层领导正在跟踪 Region Flex。

亚马逊的杂货业务将该计划描述为“S 团队目标”，指的是亚马逊的高级领导团队，并表示团队正在计划 100 多项软件迁移。 这些文件还将 Region Flex 描述为提高 AWS 中断期间的恢复能力。

全行业的人工智能热潮推动了对计算基础设施的需求飙升，而电力和可用数据中心空间已成为扩张的主要制约因素。

根据 CBRE 的数据，到 2025 年底，北美最大数据中心市场的空置率将降至创纪录的 1.4%。 有限的电力供应正在推动更多的数据中心从现有的中心转向更小的市场，在那里可以更快地获得电力。

亚马逊正在增加大量基础设施来满足需求。 10月，该公司表示，其数据中心容量比上一年增加了超过3.8吉瓦，自2022年以来其云规模增加了一倍，并预计到2027年底其电力容量将再次增加一倍左右。

分配工作负载

都柏林一直是 Region Flex 的重点之一。 爱尔兰在过去十年中成为欧洲最大的数据中心市场之一，给该国的电力系统带来了巨大的压力。

去年的一项内部计划呼吁通过到 2025 年进行迁移和弃用，将亚马逊电子商务业务在都柏林的基础设施足迹减少 40%。 它还考虑在 2026 年底之前完全撤离都柏林，并在 2029 年之前完全撤离北弗吉尼亚州和俄勒冈州的 AWS 区域。

亚马逊发言人在发给 Business Insider 的电子邮件中证实了 Region Flex 的存在。 该发言人补充说，亚马逊的官方内部文件并不总是反映当前的计划，并称《商业内幕》获得的文件中的一些时间表和其他细节“不准确”。

这位发言人表示：“发展我们的基础设施并不是什么新鲜事，多年来我们一直在这样做，以提供客户期望从亚马逊获得的体验。”

该发言人表示，使用更多的 AWS 区域可以让亚马逊的在线零售业务更加灵活地满足客户需求、提高可靠性、管理成本并使服务更贴近客户。

内部文件显示，亚马逊将工作负载从其历史悠久的都柏林中心转移，并将其分布到更多 AWS 区域，包括法兰克福和西班牙萨拉戈萨。

那可能会更贵。 根据一份文件，从都柏林转移到其他两个地区的一些服务可能会导致基础设施成本上升 10% 到 15%，因为分配工作负载会降低托管效率。 根据一份内部规划文件，亚马逊还预计 2025 年在 Region Flex 上的一次性支出将达到 9000 万美元。

分配工作负载并不一定能消除容量问题。 其中一份文件指出，萨拉戈萨地区的“容量限制”意味着该组织计划仅将剩余基础设施成本的 65% 转移到那里，将 35% 留在都柏林。

尽管AWS快速扩张，但该公司仍预计短缺现象将持续存在。 贾西称电力是去年“最大的单一制约因素”，并表示在上个月的财报电话会议上需求将继续超过供应。

Jassy 表示：“即使达到这个数量，我们仍然没有足够的产能来满足 2026 年的所有需求。”他补充说，他预计 2027 年也会出现同样的情况。
